title: Summer Car Detailing in the Cowichan Valley: Protecting Your Paint from Sun, Sap, and Gravel Dust
metaDescription: Summer car detailing in the Cowichan Valley protects paint from UV fading, tree sap, and gravel road dust. Mobile service in Duncan from $89. Call 250-709-1371.
excerpt: Long sunny days, gravel back roads, and dripping fir trees make summer tough on a vehicle's paint in the Cowichan Valley. Here's what actually protects your car through August.

content.text: By late July, most vehicles around Duncan, Cobble Hill, and Lake Cowichan are showing the same wear: chalky, dulled paint on the hood and roof, sticky sap spots under the fir and arbutus trees, and a fine layer of gravel dust baked onto every panel from trips down rural back roads. Summer is one of the hardest seasons on a car's finish here, and it's also the easiest to protect against if you catch it early.
UV Fading Is Real, and It's Cumulative

Vancouver Island summers bring long daylight hours and strong UV exposure, especially for vehicles parked outside at trailheads, at the lake, or in driveways with no shade in Mill Bay or Shawnigan Lake. Unprotected clear coat oxidizes under sustained sun, and once it does, the paint looks dull no matter how much you wash it. A coat of quality carnauba or synthetic sealant creates a sacrificial UV barrier, and it needs renewing roughly every 8-12 weeks through summer since heat and sun break it down faster than in cooler months.
Tree Sap Etches Paint Fast, and Gravel Dust Is Abrasive

The Cowichan Valley's fir, cedar, and arbutus cover means sap drips are a near-daily reality if you park under trees in Duncan, Crofton, or Cobble Hill. Sap and bird droppings are acidic and will etch through wax and into clear coat within 24-48 hours in hot weather, leaving a permanent ring even after the spot is cleaned off. Meanwhile, drivers commuting in from gravel or logging roads around Lake Cowichan, Chemainus, and Shawnigan Lake pick up a fine dust that isn't just cosmetic, it's abrasive, and a regular sponge wash grinds it straight into the clear coat as micro-scratches. Our exterior details use a foam pre-soak and two-bucket hand wash with pH-neutral soap specifically to lift that grit off before it ever touches the paint, followed by a clay bar pass to pull out anything already embedded.

items: Foam pre-soak and two-bucket pH-neutral hand wash to avoid swirl marks from gritty summer dirt
Clay bar treatment to remove embedded sap residue and road film
Machine or hand-applied UV sealant or wax for sun protection through August and September
Tire and trim dressing to stop plastic and rubber from sun-fading and cracking
Interior vacuum and UV protectant on the dash to fight heat-driven cracking
